vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: the loans given to the customer who buys the car
renting a large number of cars to companies
a finance company owned by the manufacturer
all the dealers that sell the cars of a brand
all the loans a company has, seen as one set
the credit line for the cars in the dealer showroom
to start doing something outside the original business
the share of the cars sold that the group finances

paras: Inside a large automotive group, three companies work side by side, and people who are new to the sector often confuse them. The first one is the bank. It holds the licence and provides services to the rest of the group in each country where the group operates.

The second one is the captive finance company. The word captive matters: this company was set up by the manufacturer to finance the products of the manufacturer. It works on two sides. It gives the dealer a floor plan, a credit line that pays for the cars in the showroom before any customer arrives, and it offers retail financing to the person who finally buys the car.

The third one is the rental company. It operates in fleet rental and leasing, and its clients are companies, not individual drivers. A client with two hundred cars does not want to own them or sell them three years later; it wants to use them and give them back. That is why the group branched out into rental: the same car, a different business model.

One number measures the whole system: the penetration rate, the share of the cars sold that the group itself finances. If the dealer network sells ten cars and the finance company finances four of them, the penetration rate is forty per cent. The other six go to banks outside the group.

In terms of people, the three entities are very different. The bank is small and technical, the finance company is the largest one, and the rental company is young and grows fast. Same group, three ways of working, and one HR business partner for all of them.

items.situation: A colleague asks: "What is a captive finance company?"
tips: It is a finance company owned by the manufacturer, and it finances the cars of the group.
One sentence is enough. Do not start with the history.

items.situation: She asks: "So the dealer is a client too?"
tips: Yes. We provide services to the dealer network through the floor plan.

items.situation: She asks: "What is the difference between leasing and rental?"
tips: In leasing the client uses the car for a period and gives it back; fleet rental is the same idea for a large number of cars.
Keep the client in the sentence.

items.situation: She asks: "How big is the business here?"
tips: In terms of penetration rate, we finance around forty per cent of the cars sold.
in terms of + the angle you are choosing.

items.situation: She asks: "Can you explain the structure again, more simply?"
tips: Let me break down the structure for you: three companies, three clients.

items.situation: She asks: "When did the group start renting cars?"
tips: The group branched out into rental about ten years ago.
branch out INTO a new business.

listenings.text: Camila, hi, it's Sofia from Italy. I have a call with the global team on Friday, and they asked me to present the structure in South America. I have the organisation chart, but honestly I don't understand it. Here in Italy everything is one entity, so when you say the bank, the finance company and the rental company, I don't know what each one really does, or who the clients are. Could you send me three lines, one for each company? What it does and who its clients are. Nothing long, please, three lines. If you can send it before Thursday evening, I can prepare my part on Friday morning. Thank you so much. Talk soon.

Welcome to the group. In two minutes, here is the business you have just joined. We sell cars, and around those cars we run three companies. The bank holds the licence and provides services to the whole structure. The finance company works with the dealer and with the driver: it gives the dealer a floor plan, which pays for the cars in the showroom, and it gives the customer retail financing when the car is sold. The rental company works with corporate clients who want to use cars, not to own them. One number tells you how well the system works: the penetration rate. Today it is close to forty per cent, which means four out of ten cars sold are financed by us. The other six are financed by somebody else.
